key_insight: Patch-aligned features from foundation models are highly redundant because self-attention mixes information across patches; randomly selecting fewer patches during training (stochastic patch selection) forces the policy to use non-redundant cues and improves out-of-distribution robustness.
problem_solved: Reduces excessive redundancy and over-reliance on correlated patch features in end-to-end autonomous-driving policies, improving generalization to OOD scenarios and trimming inefficient input representations.
method: Quantify redundancy in BLIP2 patch features using PCA and cross-patch similarity (≈90% redundancy).
Apply Stochastic Patch Selection (SPS): randomly sample a subset of patch-aligned features during training so the policy must learn from diverse, non-redundant signals.
Train end-to-end driving policies on reduced patch sets to improve robustness and reduce reliance on redundant descriptors.
impact: Makes end-to-end driving models more robust to distribution shifts while lowering input redundancy and potential compute/overfitting costs — valuable for practitioners building reliable autonomous driving systems with foundation-model features.
visual_elements: Schematic of self-attention mixing across image patches (patch grid with attention links) illustrating implicit redundancy.
Bar or pie chart showing quantified redundancy (≈90%) from PCA / cross-patch similarity.
Before/after diagram of Stochastic Patch Selection: full patch set → sampled subset → trained policy, highlighting robustness gains on OOD examples.
Side-by-side conceptual comparison of model behavior on in-distribution vs OOD scenarios with and without SPS.
paper_title: See Less, Drive Better: Generalizable End-to-End Autonomous Driving via Foundation Models Stochastic Patch Selection
paper_authors: Amir Mallak, Erfan Aasi, Shiva Sreeram, Tsun-Hsuan Wang, Daniela Rus
